therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus inadequately controlled on sulfonylurea (glyburide)
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 26

results.effect_size: Alogliptin 12.5 mg: -0.38% vs placebo +0.01% (difference -0.39%); Alogliptin 25 mg: -0.52% vs placebo +0.01% (difference -0.53%)
results.target_engagement_evidence: Reductions in fasting plasma glucose observed as early as Week 1; improvements in proinsulin/insulin ratio at early timepoints suggest enhanced beta-cell function
biomarker_changes: Alogliptin 12.5 mg reduced FPG by -4.7 mg/dL vs placebo +2.2 mg/dL at Week 26
Alogliptin 25 mg reduced FPG by -8.4 mg/dL vs placebo +2.2 mg/dL at Week 26
Proinsulin/insulin ratio decreased with alogliptin 12.5 mg at Weeks 4 and 8 (p<0.05 vs placebo)
C-peptide increased with alogliptin 25 mg at Week 8 (difference +0.349 ng/mL, p=0.012)
Body weight increased modestly in alogliptin arms vs placebo at Week 26 (differences ~+0.80–0.88 kg)
safety_signals: Serious adverse events were infrequent and distributed across arms
Angina pectoris reported in 2 patients in alogliptin 25 mg arm
Cardiac events (arteriosclerosis, cardiac failure, myocardial infarction) each in 1 patient in alogliptin 12.5 mg arm
Body weight increased significantly in alogliptin arms vs placebo

dose_info.schedule: once daily for up to 26 weeks

modulation_entries.hypothesis: DPP-4 inhibition by alogliptin raises active GLP-1/GIP levels, enhancing glucose-dependent insulin secretion and complementing the sulfonylurea-driven insulin release, resulting in greater glycemic lowering than glyburide alone
modulation_entries.citation: Alogliptin 12.5 mg: -0.38% and Alogliptin 25 mg: -0.52% vs placebo +0.01% change in HbA1c at Week 26 (p<0.001 for both comparisons)
